llm.summary: The skill is a coherent Cue financial-research helper, but it asks the agent to pull and run changing code from external Git repositories in the user's home directory.

dimensions.detail: Network calls to Cue and use of a Cue API key are expected for this service, and credit use is disclosed, but the external runner has broader local execution capability than the reviewed Markdown artifact itself.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The setup instructs cloning or fast-forward pulling https://github.com/sensedeal/cue-skills or https://gitee.com/sensedeal/cue-skills into ~/.cue/cue-skills, then running a Python runner from that repo, with no pinned commit or reviewed bundled code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires explicit user confirmation before spending credits and says not to fabricate empty results, but its operational flow depends on live Cue playbook data and dynamic template selection.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates or updates persistent files under ~/.cue and relies on a local Cue config/API key read by the runner; this is purpose-aligned but not tightly scoped or pinned.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is financial-report deep research using Cue, and the instructions consistently focus on public financial data analysis with source-backed reports.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the external cue-skills repository before installing, because the skill runs code that can change after this skill version was reviewed. Only proceed if you trust Cue/sensedeal, are comfortable with Chinese-language instructions, and understand that runs may consume Cue credits using your local Cue API key.
llm.findings: [SQP-3] expected: The artifact is written in Chinese and targets a Chinese Cue financial-research scene; this is a user-experience and locale disclosure issue rather than evidence of hidden or malicious behavior.
